doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Note-taking at festivals and compressing live reviews
summary: He writes a narrative of each set and compresses it into short pieces; he jokes about overused words like 'impactive' and 'underpin'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What kind of notes do you take on live music that you’re listening to so that later you can make a piece out of it?

I’m a bit of a compulsive note taker. It’s a funny process. I write, you know, like almost a little narrative of the set. And hopefully, you just kind of find a word or a phrase that just kind of pops out. And you pin that down on paper. And that can be a kicking off point for something that you actually say. I’m not going to write a piece that says at the beginning of the set he played “Indiana” and then he played — whatever. You’re trying to paint a little picture. I mean I’ve got to do two articles about this, one for a magazine called Jazzwise, I’ve got 300 words to describe a great deal of music. Right? I’ve doing another piece which will be like a color piece, as we would call it, and it’s 750 words. So it’s a powerful process of compression, isn’t it? What you do, you’re just trying to find that little phrase which leaves some idea, a picture of what we’re about, what actually occurred. But you can’t, there’s no way you can describe it piece by piece.
Do you have any favorite adjectives?
Impactive. I find impactive I’m using rather too often recently.
Um. We all have our own cliches you know. My other one is “underpin.” If you read my stuff, the word “underpin” appears too often.
